summary.headline: KFin Q1 FY27 revenue grew 30% YoY to consolidate Ascent (ex-Ascent ~10%), while PAT was flat-to-down and EBITDA margin fell to 34.2% with Ascent.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 30% YoY, with about 9.6% growth excluding Ascent, and 2.7% QoQ including Ascent (1.6% excluding). EBITDA grew about 7.1% YoY, but consolidated EBITDA margin was 34.2% with Ascent versus 39.4% without it. PAT margin was 21% including Ascent and 26.6% excluding it, and PAT was broadly flat to marginally down YoY. Management raised its FY27 growth outlook to EBITDA growth of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, while a yield decline of about 2% QoQ in mutual funds was attributed to debt-to-liquid mix shift and provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

financial_highlights.change: About INR 200 crore to go to dividend already declared

financial_highlights.value: About 51% of EBITDA converted to free cash flow

financial_highlights.change: from US$5.7 million in Q4; US$4.4 million in Q1 FY26 (pre-consolidation), +32% YoY

segments.name: Domestic mutual fund (RTA/fund admin)
segments.commentary: Industry AUM grew about 15% YoY versus KFin about 16%; KFin's equity AUM market share rose about 80 bps QoQ. Yield fell about 2% QoQ, of which about 30% was debt-to-liquid mix and the rest mainly provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

segments.name: Issuer solutions
segments.commentary: Managed about 80% of main-board IPO issue size in Q1 and holds about 50% of NSE 500 market share (versus ~52% earlier). Corporate actions are about 30% of issuer revenue; the company guided to tepid corporate actions in Q2 due to IT services dividend deferrals.

segments.name: International (Ascent and global fund solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 200% YoY with Ascent and about 32% organically. Ascent EBITDA margin was about 8%; management targets double-digit margin within 12 months. Sequential decline ex-Ascent was attributed to pipeline timing, with growth expected above 25%.

segments.name: Alternatives (XAlt, GIFT City)
segments.commentary: About 731 funds with about 37.3% market share, targeting close to 40% with pending launches. 15 new AIF wins in Q1; the AIF business has compounded above 60% over four years and management expects at least 40% growth going forward.

segments.name: Pensions (NPS)
segments.commentary: Reached break-even last quarter and now contributes about 15%+ EBITDA margin. Manages about 2.5 million pensioners and is the second-largest CRA in India.

segments.name: Wealth management (mPower Wealth) and technology
segments.commentary: Three wealth platform mandates won. An INR 25 crore+ big-data mandate runs over about 18 months, with INR 40 crore of signed bolt-on deals across 3-15 month durations.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR guided at 18-20%, unchanged from prior guidance.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 40-45%; management aims to hold 40% threshold including Ascent by end of FY27.
FY27 visibility of EBITDA growth of about 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, ahead of the earlier high-single to low-double-digit indication.
Ascent to become EBITDA accretive by end-FY27 or early FY28; double-digit margin targeted within the next 12 months; KFin-level EBITDA margin expansion to take three to five years.
Cost optimisation benefits expected from Q2 FY27 onwards; mutual fund yield expected to stabilise, with management unwilling to guide a yield number.
Target of at least 20% of revenue from controllable (non-market) businesses; currently about 6% from VAS plus 5-6% from other non-market businesses.
capex_capacity: Ascent cost base is being rationalised through shared support functions, consolidated office space and better vendor contracts (AWS, Oracle, Microsoft); contract renewals roll into KFin structures in October and January.

Mutual fund platform transformation under FinEx: SIP processing now completes within three working days for 99.7% of transactions (versus about 21 days industry); next launch by end-calendar 2026 to automate non-commercial and purchase transactions.
Cayman Islands facility being set up to meet regulatory substance requirements, a near-term cost already in the plan.
Infrastructure cost pressure (servers, routers, laptops) noted; management will be harder on client discount negotiations.
demand_pricing: Mutual fund yield fell about 2% QoQ: debt-to-liquid shift (debt yields 2-2.5x liquid) contributed about 30% of the decline, and provisioning for a large-contract renewal this year accounted for the rest. Management guides against a fixed yield number, citing asset-mix and AMC-growth effects.
Ascent revenue hit by digital-asset fund markdowns, offset by six new fund managers with over US$100 million each (transitions taking 3-5 months) and fund launches.

Retail participation is still weak, with Demat net additions slowing despite IPOs; IPO pipeline includes PhonePe, Zepto, Jio, Manipal Health and Razorpay, plus Razorpay, Garuda and Pushp Brand mandates won.
Management expects strong corporate actions outside IT services; IT services firms have deferred dividends, which could weigh on Q2.
Pending Philippines government contract: KFin is reported as highest bidder on technical and commercial scores, but no award has been announced.
